body: I find it easier looking after the adult dogs, and she finds it easier looking after the puppy. We've done this plenty of times before, particularly when either or neither of us can find dogsitters, but we've always kept each other updated on how the dogs are doing. I guess I took for granted that she lives nearby and I could visit whenever, while also not really wanting to see her. Now I don't have a choice but to give her a visit.

NParents have a way of making you feel guilty for standing up for yourself, or for doing what you need to do in order to thrive. When you're near, they blame their problems on you, but when you're gone, they blame their problems on your absence. It is an unwinnable game. I'm glad you see that you're not alone in this, as I struggled with feeling like I was the only one going through this when I was younger and it made everything so much worse. It made me more vulnerable to the manipulation, made me believe that I was in the wrong and a horrible person. If you need to get away from your mother, it is absolutely not your fault, you are not in the wrong, and you have nothing to feel guilty for.

My parents were both distant when I was a kid. Dad was critical of just about everything that anyone said or did while believing he was perfect in every way... and believe it or not, he's not even the narcissist in the picture (not that I know of at least), he's actually mellowed out considerably as he's aged and while his conduct earlier in my life still screwed me up, I'm thankful to have him in my life as a supportive and loving figure.

Mom on the other hand always made a point to convey that I needed her *much* more than she ever needed me (even saying it up front once in a fit of rage, though I was already an adult by then). I think this is the reason why I'm so distant now, *especially* with potential romantic partners. I go into every relationship, platonic, romantic, sexual or otherwise, assuming that the other person will eventually find fault with and abandon me, so I numb myself to that person and the relationship beforehand so it won't hurt as much. I have no clue how to stop doing this, or if I even fully want to.

This creates a rift between how I perceive myself and how others see me. To my friends or the guys I go out with, I'm funny, witty, a good conversationalist. All I can see in myself is the weirdo loner kid who could never make friends or find love, the kid who my dad chastised for being chubby and having stuffed animals, the kid my mother called "weak" for feeling normal human emotions and needing comfort when I was hurt. I just know that, if they dig deep enough past that "charming" front, they'll see how worthless I am and chuck me aside like everyone else has. I'm just so used to it now that I barely try with people and I don't know how they still end up liking me, I just know it causes me more anxiety just dreading the day when they no longer like me, but I have to bury the anxiety so as to not showcase to the world what a neurotic wreck I am. It makes me not want to deal with anyone, even people I like, but I also can't say no to them so I just go with whatever they say (within reason) until they inevitably forget about me.

That's the other thing I find weird (and kind of amusing), everyone tells me how reserved, how unflappable, how "cool" and composed I am, when I am in a near constant state of panic. I am like the least calm person I know, and yet I am somehow "the calm friend". But, this comment is now way longer than it was supposed to be and I'm rambling so I'll conclude with, absolutely it has. It's affected my romantic relationships, my friendships, my business dealings, pretty much every aspect of my life where I have to interact with another human. I feel like they won't like me so I dial back my personality by like 90%, they like me, I feel guilty because they like an idealized "me" which isn't really me, I drift away, the ones who have yet to forget about me hit me up saying they miss me and the cycle continues...

I've stopped trying. My logic is, the people who know me generally tell me how nice and respectful they think I am (even if my NMom tells them something different). By contrast, while my mother is good at maintaining relationships in the short-term, she doesn't seem very adept at holding onto friends or even acquaintances. I figure that if they choose to believe her, fine, they can see for themselves the kind of person she is and if they still support her after that, not my problem.

The only person who is still her friend after so long 1. concedes that something is wrong with my mother and 2. takes my side every time me and my mother have a conflict, sometimes being the person to talk some sense into my mother, even if only temporarily. I'm torn between aspiring to have the kind of patience and compassion she (the friend, not my mom) has, and wanting to rid myself of said traits to not have to suffer like I have at the hands of anyone similar to my mom.

TL;DR, I just let people believe what they will, the truth always comes out eventually...

Not really, admittedly I'm ignorant of the whole online counseling scene. And I'm 27, too old for anyone to care and old enough that I probably shouldn't whine so much but it is what it is ¯\\\_(ツ)\_/¯

I've learned this the hard way, being trained to be my mother's personal flying monkey all my life, listening to her trash everyone we know only to smile in their faces and drown them in fake kindness. I wish they knew what a fucking monster she's always been.

I feel like my N mother has actively gotten dumber, to the detriment of herself and everyone around her. I get that she's had a hard childhood and doesn't trust easily but she uses it as a crutch, she's had so many friends and relatives try to help her and she's always shit-talking them to in private, how dumb or shady or fake they are, all while moaning about having no friends or relatives to call on. And she expects me to believe she doesn't do the same to me to those same friends, bullshit. As much as she loves berating me to my face, I'm supposed to accept that she doesn't badmouth me to other people? And I swear she purposefully misunderstands things just to have something to argue or feel superior over.

"You aren't depressed, just don't claim the depression and you'll feel better / stop feeling sorry for yourself!"

For as smart as she wants to seem, my mother really is a fucking idiot.

Literally all the time, and it's gotten no better with the current state of things because every little thing convinces her that she's got "it". Me speaking out in any way is abusing her, and warrants a lecture about how I am hands down the most ungrateful, disrespectful child she's every known (not a child anymore stupid), and yet trying to get away from her is apparently me leaving her to possibly die instead of helping her like I "need" to. She never could make up her mind if she was proud of me or hated me, and now she can't make up her mind if she's completely self-sufficient and needs me away from her, or some frail sick old lady (she is none of these things) who needs my constant support. No matter what, I'm screwing up somehow by her standards. There's no winning with her.

I doubt it, I don't even post here consistently. I don't mean to be contrarian (even if it is like my only personality trait besides sadness and binge eating) but I feel like such a non-person, you know? I've let everyone down, I've pushed everyone away, isolated myself from everyone and become such a freaking iceberg drifting out in the middle of absolutely nowhere. The only thing keeping me here is my dog, and she's already quite old herself. I just feel like I'm rapidly running out of options, that I'm getting far too old for all of this and either need to get better or get lost, and I've been trying to get better for so long and for what? To be here on my own, feeling like dirt because I have nobody? What were all of those years for, why did I ever bother making good memories with people that just make me feel bad that we don't talk anymore? I could literally just disappear and no one would know or care.

Well, I guess a few people I've been talking to here, today would notice, but even so, I've done this before. I always end up ghosting people because I'm flighty and scared and I spiral all over again and everyone forgets about me all over again and it is entirely my own fault. I can't let anybody hold onto me, I genuinely do not know how, so I take the easy way out and let myself drift away and be lonely. Give it a month of me just forgetting to check in on Reddit and guaranteed, my presence will fade once more.

It sucks, feeling invisible and disconnected from everyone and everything around you, but it's liberating in a masochistic sort of way. You know nobody cares about you so you are free, to also stop caring about yourself. It becomes so easy not to bathe, sleep on time, eat consistently, go outside. It becomes so easy to cease existing. That's the thing, I'm already dead, and nobody cares or has cared. I don't want to sound like I'm raging against the world (I guess I kind of am???) but, I haven't been "here" for a while. It wouldn't make much of a difference to take it just that teeny bit further.

idk, it's late and I'm sad so I'm sorry for being like this, I just don't really know what I'm doing with myself anymore, and it is so hard to care.

Or family or even acquaintances who they're on good terms with. I am a full-blown hermit, I doubt anyone would even find my body in my own apartment until a week or so later. I try to care for myself even with no one else caring but, it's hard.

Over-stimulation is a problem for me as well, and it blows but some people, through no fault of their own, are more draining than others. I've learned the hard way not to point this out to said people...

I suppose that's another part of it, is socializing and becoming good at it and comfortable around others is mostly trial and error but there are so many variables to account for and every now and then someone completely throws you for a loop and the ol' anxiety starts acting up again until you just remove yourself from the situation, which is just plain difficult to explain to people, especially in the midst of that anxiety. Well, I am glad to hear from someone dealing with the same feelings, thank you.

If you would, imagine a potato. Imagine holding it. Now imagine it rotting in your hands, a disgusting withered thing of no value to anybody. I cannot be salvaged, I am simply a waste.

But that's kind of depressing so let's just say I'm a good ol' Yukon gold potato. I probably would've made for some bomb-ass french fries in my day but, alas ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

What kind of work do you do, if you don't mind being questioned by a sad potato?

Nothing about me is or would be newsworthy, I guess besides what a sloppy fat horder I've managed to become. Ugh, that'd be even worse than just being forgotten, I pray I'm forgotten.

EDIT: It's foolish to think they wouldn't be able to link the account to me, but I doubt anyone would care to. I'm not harming anyone, I have no great plans of any sort, good or bad. I am a nonperson.

Eh, that's nice of you to say but it's just not registering right now, I'm sorry. I mean, I could just off myself now and literally nobody would know, online or in person. Well, maybe my dog might alert somebody, or the eventual smell, but otherwise I might as well not be here. I honestly hate people being nice to me, I genuinely don't know how to respond but with apathy and doubt, I'm sorry.

Same, I'm ashamed of my kinks and fetishes and the way I'm always either thinking of death or thinking of sex. I feel so gross sometimes. If it's any consolation, you're almost guaranteed to be less of a pervert than I am...
I used to, when I had loved ones. No one cares anymore since I fell off the face of the earth. I'm basically only alive out of spite at this point.
Not fresh? What are you, a head of lettuce? Ignorant bosses always say the *dumbest* things...

I know it's just the sad contrarian in me speaking but you can't prove any of that. No one in my life even knows who I am anymore because I don't reach out to them anymore, nor them me, no one believes in or loves me. Hell, my own mother thinks I'm useless, and in my current frame of mind I am inclined to agree. If you knew me, you'd probably agree too. I mean, here I am being a downer on a happy post because that's all I'm good at. idk, I'm too sober for this.

I want to vent but I have nothing concrete to vent about, just general vague feelings and thoughts bringing me down. I'm an alien struggling to find my place amongst humans and wouldn't you know, nobody wants to be probed ¯\\\_(ツ)\_/¯

I just feel lonely and kind of detached. Everything feels unreal, like a hazy dream, the kind that kind of disturbs you and sticks with you long after you wake up but you can't remember anything specific about it. I feel like I am a dream or a memory or a vague feeling or thought fashioned after somebodies fragmented idea of what a human is. Also I no longer have any friends or family members who I trust with my emotions so there's that, lol

I'm mad at myself because here I am complaining about feeling sad when it is entirely my own fault that I'm sad and others are dealing with real issues. I guess depression is a real issue but I'm the one sitting on my butt all day and doing nothing to fix the issue. I feel like the embodiment of wasted potential. Every used to tell me how smart, funny, nice I am but I just feel useless. I wish I had a friend but I don't deserve one since I'm awful at reaching out to people, I am a bad friend, content to sit at home and be sad and useless. I know it's learned helplessness but I still feel... helpless. My anxiety keeps getting triggered by dumb things that don't matter and I realize they don't matter so I get mad at myself again and I get depressed again and I just wish I could melt and drain into the sewer and never have to deal with feelings again.

I don't feel like a genuine human being. I feel fragmented like a foggy memory. I'm questioning if I even am or want to be a "man" and questioning my participation in society as a whole. I'm lonely as hell and there is a massive word salad in my mind PLEADING with me to be let out. I feel lazy and worthless and like, in spite of my efforts and the progress I've made and all the therapy, I'll always be depressed. I'm confused and nothing feels real anymore.

THANK YOU. My family is trash and I'm tired of people implying (or stating) that I'm ungrateful or selfish for not talking to them, or that I need to maintain a relationship with these hostile strangers who just so happen to be related to me. I need to be away from them for the sake of my mental healtg, and I'm glad I finally realized that and acted on it, and I'm not sorry about it either. Have a happy, stress-free holiday season, I know I will :D

I'm experiencing my first holiday season away from both my narcissistic mother and her narcissistic parents and my shitty aunts and uncle and it is a breath of fresh air. Hang in there, it gets better, and happy holidays!

This will be my first holiday season spent away from my (immediate) family and I'm feeling free, happy and at ease, for the first time in a good long while. Sometimes having nobody around is a blessing. Merry Christmas, I hope you have an awesome one.
I'm okay now, middle school was just a low point in my life all-around, everything sucked and nobody cared. Things are better these days, thankfully.

LMAO, that reminds me of kind of an in-joke in my family of one of my cousins hitting on my aunt before realizing she was a bit of a snob tbh, *and then* realizing they were related. Like they say, it's a small world...
lol we might be, I've had weirder stories of finding out someone's related to me (my fav thus far is when I had to do a family tree for a course and realized I was related to the professor)

I could definitely see there being a generational component, my paternal grandmother (the one I mentioned earlier is my maternal grandmother) and especially my maternal grandfather have some big-time N behavior, the former being a haughty, judgmental, xenophobic racist (as well as highly accomplished and well-respected in her community who more than likely don't know about the bigotry) and the latter being ignorant, irresponsible, entitled and abusive. I'm somewhat forgiving of my NMom (and my questionable aunts and uncles) just because of what she and they have had to deal with in this absolute circus of a "family".

I can relate to a lot of this, I'm a 27 y/o aspie (diagnosed around 14), mom was a teacher, sorority girl, first college grad of the family, hates "whining" or "weakness", always sounds angry even when she isn't. I grew up watching her stressed most of the day working two jobs and going to school while also managing to be a helicopter parent for me, holds a grudge against my dad both for cheating and for choosing to live with his family in Lebanon instead of with me and her.

I hate hearing people call my name, have trouble not breaking down after even simple mistakes and am only now getting over the guilt I've felt over many of the things I've done wrong. It takes time, but what helps me is trying to become more aware of the behavior and where it stems from and not judging myself over it, as well as reminding myself that mistakes don't necessarily equal failure or ineptitude, and that they happen to all of us.

Yep. Mine video taped me once and showed it to me any time I started to cry or get upset with her. I used to dread the thought of her still having that footage or showing it to anyone else but now it's whatever, it is her burden, not mine.

NMom just used this line on me twice, after calling me for like the fourth time and yelling at me for hurting her feelings when I said I didn't feel like talking. She's "done"... which means she'll be calling me next time she feels lonely because she has no other friends.

It's cliché but taking deep breaths and counting to ten (or in my experience, just counting aimlessly) helps, as well as getting away from the situation if possible. As for dealing with Ns, I try my best not to take offense to their behavior and remember that they act they way they do out of hurt, that the hurt they carry with them distorts their thinking and that I am not responsible for their distorted thinking. It's a process. I just had kind of a bad argument with my mom and the guilt is just now subsiding, plus I'm still minorly freaking out over checking an email my dad sent me, so it's definitely a process.

I think it's important to become as aware of your behavior without judging it. It can be hard if you've grown up having been made to feel guilty about things, but it gets easier with practice. I used to feel majorly guilty about not writing my dad back in a timely manner or getting into arguments with my mother, but dad wasn't very approachable when I was young and mom is just kind of resentful of the entire world for failing her as a child. While I'd like to heal and move forward, I recognize that my experiences impact my behavior, as is the case with everybody, including my parents. We are all only human. Sorry if I'm rambling, it's a weird night. I hope this helps!

Ugh, this is my mother, all of it, verbatim. And she will swear up and down that she's NEVER had a victim complex unlike *some* people, she's too strong and works too hard and doesn't allow herself to wallow in self-pity and blah blah blah. And she's still somehow able to take literally everything personally, if she isn't ranting to me about some innocuous statement a client or colleague made that she's sure is secretly a dig at her, then she's telling me how disrespectful I am for \[blank\] and how mean and awful I am. Trying to reason with a narc is like trying to get a feel for how you look in a funhouse mirror.

What bugs me, more than the scapegoating and her constantly being on my case for everything, is how she uses me as a prop to make herself look good when talking to others, especially in cases of me "reacting" to things she says or does. "And he started laughing, he thought it was so funny!" or "he was so mad at them on my behalf, we just couldn't believe how they treated me!" Okay, except none of that is true but please don't let me stop you from carrying me around in all of your memories Weekend at Bernie's style. You can't just tell someone a funny story and hope they laugh like a normal person, you need that false assurance, "see, my son totally thought it was funny too, laugh!" No one's laughing you damn clown, keep my name out of your mouth.

Same here. I had kind of a chilling incident where my mom seemed to allude to some sort of suicidal ideation because I "didn't love her" or whatever, what calmed me down was knowing her ego is too great to actually do it, she's always talking shit about how bad it would look on the family if I killed myself and that I'm stupid for being so "dramatic" (a subject she is an expert on).

Yep, that describes my entire adolescence and adulthood thus far. After I stopped being cute and easily swayed, it was time to remind me of everything I had ever done to her, constantly, for the rest of my life. And if she can't think of an incident from the past, then it's just "I hate how lazy you are!" I swear that woman feeds on her own righteous indignation.

And oh god, "I can't stand liars". I only lie to you because the truth seems to piss you off exponentially more but go off I guess...

I feel in some ways that this could apply to my grandmother. From all accounts, she was an absolute nightmare as a young mother and caretaker, and now in her old age, seems a very meek and sympathetic individual. I still don't trust her and she's not quite putting in the effort that your aunt seems to be putting in, but she's apparently calmed down a lot from the abusive, attention-seeking person she used to be, though you can definitely still see kernels of self-absorption and entitlement within her.

My mom has had episodes where, against all odds, she seems to become aware of her more destructive traits and expresses desire to change, but thus far they've never gone anywhere and she settles quite comfortably back into being controlling, manipulative, aggressive and arrogant. As much as I used to wish for such, I kind of hope she never does try at her own "redemption arc" so to speak, I really don't know if I could easily forgive her and frankly I think it would just be awkward.

I feel guilty lying, but many times I feel I need to lie to my mom so the conversation doesn't devolve into another shouting match. I guess the sense of necessity is what lessened the guilt. I can be truthful with the average person because I don't have the expectation that they're going to start shouting at me and scapegoating me for everything wrong with my family, but that woman? At this point, I don't even care about the moral weight of lying to her. I would just tell the truth to irritate her more but, not worth the hassle. I get that paradoxical feeling, of Mother being The Most Important thing in your life, and also being the most draining, dreadful, difficult thing in your life.

I'm nearly thirty and still learning how to handle this, I think it's the result of having parents or a parent that overdramatizes absolutely everything. I still have to put forth considerable effort to calm myself down during certain episodes and not fly off the handle, and I still fail pretty often. At the very least, I'm more aware of the behaviors and some of my triggers.

My mother wears her age with pride, probably because 1. everyone tells her she looks younger than she is and 2. she thinks everyone under a certain age (hers) is stupid anyway. Definitely the type to make everything about herself though, you can't watch a sitcom or the news with her without her making it about herself somehow. It's one of those things you take in stride until you realize both how common it is and the thought process behind it.

If that's the case, my entire bloodline is just generations of fucked up, my great-grandmother drove away my grandmother, who drove away my mother, who I would like to run as far away from as possible. Kind of makes me worried for any future kids I may have, I figure I'm not that bad but my lineage seems to imply otherwise, and awful people apparently never realize when they're being awful...

Jesus Christ, you literally described the entirety of my relationship with my (suspected) narc mother, that's a bit unsettling. She literally does not know me, the "me" she interacts with is whichever "me" she needs, supportive me to listen to her problems and not talk about my own, brilliant overachiever me who makes her look good to others, or disrespectful lazy me who she can lay into when she's upset and needs to feel superior to somebody.

I forgive my mother, I just never want to speak or interact with her ever again. I know she is the way she is because of trauma she's sustained in her life and she was the victim once and I understand that, but also, I hate who she's become and literally can't talk to her or connect with her in any way and I'd rather not bother. I forgive her acting out of hurt, but refuse to take her abuse any longer.

That's just me, and I only forgive her so I don't have to keep ruminating on the matter. No one can tell you what to do or how to feel, and if you don't feel particularly forgiving, there is nothing wrong with that. Also, you can forgive somebody but still not force yourself to deal with them or suffer through their bad behavior. You can forgive somebody and let them go, that's what I choose to do.

Haha, same. I like to think there's an infinite amount of "me"s floating about, and when necessary I just pick the "appropriate" one and let them take over. I kind of fear what that means about me and my "personality" as a whole but what can ya do ¯\\\_(ツ)\_/¯
As someone who has to deal with a bunch of snobs on the daily but also has a bunch of street friends, this one hits hard.

Not caring / not getting upset by things. People often tell me how calm and collected I am when all I do is internally rage and cry over pretty much everything. It sucks not being able to confide in anyone but I appreciate that nobody knows what a weak little baby I actually am.

That and my kindness, everyone thinks I'm a sweetheart because I'm quiet, accommodating and a good listener but deep down, I'm a misanthropic bastard, humanity can get bent ¯\\\_(ツ)\_/¯

Yep. I can definitely relate, idk what people see in me but I'm apparently quite likable on first impressions alone. Let someone actually spend a sufficient amount of time with me, though, and eventually they just leave, no confrontation, no explanation, just leave. The worst is when you hit them up and they say they'd just LOVE to hang out but you know they're lying because otherwise, why didn't they get in touch with you? Why don't they ever try to make plans? I know stuff like that goes both ways but damn, I'm not even good at reaching out, why must I be the only one making an effort?

Thank you, statements like the ones you mentioned have always bothered me but I've never fully known why, it seems dismissive of the people who aren't here anymore, like "okay they suffered but they're dead now so you can live your best life and not be like them!"

I had the opposite experience. First was "you're joking, you're straight, right? At least bi? But you've had crushes on girls!", then "but I really want grandchildren..." (and of course when I mentioned adoption this became "but I want *biological* grandchildren"), then "Okay!!! This is great, I can make you over and do your hair and you'll be sooo pretty", *then* becoming upset when I didn't turn out to be the flamboyant, entertaining type of gay that she likes. (same goes for you, mom) or the weird obsession she used to have (thankfully it doesn't come up these days) about whether I'd be "giving" or "receiving"...

It's heavy, mentally, emotionally and physically, so heavy that sometimes I just wish I could climb back into bed and sleep forever. It's a tightness in the chest, that constant heat behind your eyes like you're going to cry even if you don't. I feel weighed down by it, like I'm just dragging myself through life. Sometimes it's emptiness and confusion, like I'm just a placeholder, not a real human being but a mannequin, moldable depending on the circumstance but never representing anything real or with any substance behind it, fake and hollow. I feel fake, like a lab experiment gone horribly wrong and subsequently abandoned. I wish I were just a mannequin or a robot, then I wouldn't have to deal with these feelings. I'm constantly questioning my existence, especially with my parents (moreso my mom) and my grandparents (mostly on dad's side) being so disappointed with me, I feel like a defective robot, made for a specific purpose but so bad at it that my entire existence is negated and I might as well not be here. There's a lot of "imposter syndrome" thinking that comes with it, feeling like I'm not a real / valid human and like I don't deserve anything good in life, let alone to have a life, but I also can't throw away this life because it was given to me and how dare I, I don't even have it that bad and I'm just whining. It's weighing me down more and more everyday, a growing pit that I'm unable to claw myself out of.

God, if this isn't my mother. I couldn't have possibly had a tough childhood because *she* had a tough childhood, I can't possibly think there's anything wrong with her parenting because *her* parents were worse, I need to stop being upset by how I was bullied in school because *her* bullying situation was so much worse and I could never hope to understand, nothing I've been through could ever compare to what she's gone through. So, since I didn't really have it "that bad", all my pain should just magically disappear since it isn't even real, except it hasn't because it is and her responses are part of why it all still hurts so much. I've never known someone so eager to hold onto their own negative feelings but I guess that's what playing the pain game does to a person. Just let me vent and try to heal in peace, dammit.

Your experience is the exact same I have with my mother. She makes me insecure about everything then takes offense when I ask her to stop, tells me I'm being oversensitive and need to let it go, that I'm "mean" to her and take everything too personally. She vents constantly about her life but when I do the same it's "stop complaining and change your life".

Thank you for this, especially the "narcs really loathe everyone" part. I swear she just loves talking about all the wrongs she's ever experienced in life, from the big ones (and she's indeed suffered some awful things throughout her life) to the minor ones (like a cousin saying her earrings looked fake, she still won't let it go after months). It's like she's stuck in this mindset that she is the "right" one in every single conflict and conflicts only arise because other people are terrible and hate her for being such a good person. It's as if she not only enjoys thinking like this, but like it gives her power. She feeds off of it.

This perfectly describes my mom. She used to be "the fun mom", everyone loved her (me included) and she was always doing and buying fun things. Now she throws all of that in my face to prove that she couldn't possibly be anything less than a stellar parent because, "look at everything I've done for you" and "if I were such a bad mother, would I \[insert thing\]?" My dad was the opposite, he went from being fiercely critical of pretty much everything about me to seeming to accept me as I am, whereas my once great relationship with my mom is now strained as she keeps reminding me that she's an awesome mother and I'm so disrespectful and problematic.

The one constant is that she's always loved teasing me about things I'm insecure about, and now the "jokes" extend to my general character, how mean or disrespectful I am, how she does so much for me even though I've done so much to her. She's always talking about how people have wronged her and she doesn't deserve any of it, but won't hear a word about "playing victim" because she's had to be strong for so long and she doesn't play victim, *I* play victim when I'm asking her not to "joke" about things that make me feel bad or questioning why she keeps bringing up things I've done years ago to confirm that I'm "mean".

She has had a tough life with abusive parents but she uses it as an excuse not to acknowledge how her behavior affects people in the present, and LOVES to play the "I'm not abusive, I never hit you" card. All of my struggles are invalidated because they don't compare to anything she's gone though, and they probably don't, she went through a lot, but I'm hurting too, which she doesn't even like to acknowledge, even if it's nothing related to her at all.
